I **wouldn’t give Wiggle & Snug Snug-Fit Diapers a clear “yes” for a newborn unless you can verify the basics**, because I couldn’t find reliable official product information for that exact brand/name. For newborns, fit and skin-friendliness matter more than the “snug-fit” claim.

**They may be okay for a newborn if:**
- They come in a true **Newborn** size for your baby’s weight — or **Preemie** if baby is under ~6 lb; some standard newborn diapers may be too loose for very small babies. ([pampers.com](https://www.pampers.com/en-us/baby/newborn/article/preemie-diapers?utm_source=openai))  
- They fit **snugly but not tightly**: no leg/waist gaps, no red marks, tabs fasten comfortably, and leaks/blowouts are rare. ([support.pampers.com](https://support.pampers.com/hc/en-us/articles/21678052813597-How-can-I-prevent-diaper-leakage-and-protect-my-baby-s-skin?utm_source=openai))  
- They don’t rub the **umbilical cord stump**; until it falls off, the diaper should sit below it or be folded down. ([healthychildren.org](https://www.healthychildren.org/English/tips-tools/Symptom-Checker/IFrame/Pages/symptomviewer.aspx?symptom=Umbilical+Cord+Symptoms&utm_source=openai))  
- They’re **fragrance-free / gentle for sensitive skin**, since newborn skin is delicate and diaper rash prevention depends on minimizing irritation and changing diapers often. ([healthychildren.org](https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/diapers-clothing/Pages/Diaper-Rash.aspx?utm_source=openai))  

**I’d be cautious if** the package doesn’t list materials, size/weight range, fragrance/lotions, or safety/testing info. If you already have them, try a **small pack only**, check after each change for redness or leaks, and stop using them if you notice rash, chafing, or frequent blowouts.

If you send me a photo/link of the exact diaper package or ingredient list, I can help you judge it more specifically.
